_meta.purpose: Map Metaphysics book-letters (and their traditional book-numbers) to Bekker page sub-ranges. The Metaphysics is very often cited by GREEK BOOK-LETTER rather than bare Bekker (e.g. 'Metaph. Gamma 4', 'Met. Lambda 7', 'Z 1028a'). The parser needs to (a) recognise a book-letter token adjacent to 'Metaph.', and (b) validate/derive the Bekker range for that book.
_meta.critical_offset_note: The book-NUMBER vs book-LETTER mapping is OFFSET by the 'little alpha' (Book II). Sequence: Book I = Alpha (big A); Book II = alpha (little, 'alpha elatton'); Book III = Beta; Book IV = Gamma; ... So book-letter Gamma = Book IV, NOT Book III. A parser that assumes letter-position == book-number will be off by one from Beta onwards. This is a classic error source.
_meta.letter_forms_note: Book-letters appear as: Greek letter (Α Β Γ Δ Ε Ζ Η Θ Ι Κ Λ Μ Ν), transliteration (Alpha, Beta, Gamma...), or Latin-alphabet equivalent (A, B, G, D, E, Z, H, Th, I, K, L, M, N). The little alpha (Book II) is written 'alpha elatton', 'α ελαττον', 'little alpha', 'A minor', or '2'. All forms must map to the same book.
_meta.VERIFY: Bekker starts are cross-checked against The-Philosophy.com book summary and corroborated at several boundaries by Perseus (Gamma ends / Delta begins 1012b; Alpha 980a-993a; Zeta begins 1028a). Exact a/b COLUMN hand-offs at boundaries are approximate and flagged verified:false - confirm against Ross OCT or Index Aristotelicus before publication. The page integers themselves are reliable.

books.notes: Alpha ('big alpha'). 980a-993a. History of predecessors, four causes, critique of Plato's Forms.
LITTLE alpha ('alpha elatton', Book II). 993a-995a. THE offset source. Often cited 'alpha', 'α ελαττον', 'little alpha', 'Met. II'. Short book.

Gamma. 1003a-1012b. Being qua being; defence of Principle of Non-Contradiction (1005b-1006a) - a BOILERPLATE-cited passage (memo's caveat: high frequency here = settled/canonical, not contested). Perseus confirms Gamma->Delta boundary at 1012b.

Delta. 1012b-1025a. The 'philosophical lexicon' - definitions of ~30 terms (cause, nature, one, being...). Often cited for individual term-definitions, e.g. 'Delta 8' on substance. Perseus confirms Delta begins 1012b.
Epsilon. 1025a-1028a. Hierarchy of sciences; being per accidens; being as truth.
Zeta. 1028a-1041b. Substance (ousia) - one of the most heavily cited books in all Aristotle. Perseus confirms Zeta begins 1028a; Z 1 ends ~1028b.
Iota. 1052a-1059a. Unity, the one and the many. CAUTION: Latin 'I' collides with book-number 'I' (Alpha) - prefer Greek/translit forms; disambiguate by Bekker range.
Kappa. 1059a-1069a. Recapitulation of Beta-Gamma-Epsilon plus Physics excerpts. Authenticity partly doubted.
Lambda. 1069a-1076a. Theology; the Prime/Unmoved Mover (1072b) - heavily cited. Often studied/cited as a standalone. Note dokumen.pub flags text 'safe up to Λ 7 1073a1'.
Mu. 1076a-1087b. Philosophy of mathematics; critique of Forms and Numbers.
Nu. 1087a-1093b. Continues critique of Platonist/Pythagorean number-metaphysics. Last book; ends ~1093b.

_parser_guidance: A citation like 'Metaph. Γ 4 1006a' gives redundant info: the letter (Gamma), a chapter (4), and a Bekker number (1006a). Use the Bekker number as PRIMARY (it self-locates via bekker_ranges), and use the book-letter as a CONSISTENCY CHECK: 1006 should fall in Gamma's 1003-1012. Mismatch => flag for review (possible OCR/typo).

A citation like 'Met. Λ 7' gives letter + chapter but NO Bekker number. Here the book-letter is the ONLY locator - map Lambda -> 1069-1076 so it still lands on the heatmap at book resolution (not passage resolution). Track these as 'book-level only' cites, coarser than Bekker-precise ones.
Do NOT trust letter-position as book-number: Gamma is Book IV not III (little-alpha offset). Always map via this table.
Bare Greek capitals (Α Β Γ...) appear in running text for many reasons; only treat as a Metaphysics book-letter when adjacent to a Metaphysics abbreviation OR to a Bekker number in 980-1093.
